title: The Homecoming of Route 9
premise: Isandro Oyelaran, a seventeen-year-old coder in the fading town of Marrow Creek, runs an anonymous local gossip account that has become the town's conscience—and its most dangerous secret. When his college essay prompt asks 'What do you owe the place that raised you?', his honest answer accidentally exposes truths about Route 9, the century-old tradition of lantern-lit homecoming that the town council plans to cancel to make way for a development deal. As Isandro's two lives collide—his anonymous account, his scholarship ambitions, and his growing love for Priya Chandrasekaran, the councilwoman's daughter assigned to 'fix' the tradition's image—he must choose between a future he coded for himself and the found family that built him. The story ends at prom, where Isandro publicly claims both his identity and his account, rallying the town to save Route 9 not as nostalgia but as a promise to everyone still trying to come home.
about_author: Kestrel Zhou grew up in a string of small towns along highway corridors, collecting the stories of people who stayed and people who left. Their fiction explores the quiet heroism of teenagers who refuse to let their hometowns be erased.

chapters.title: The Account That Knows
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. We meet him at 3 a.m., posting as @route9ghost, exposing that the diner where his foster mom Rosa works is being quietly bought out. He counts down 214 days to graduation. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being everyone's voice and no one's name.

chapters.title: Essay Prompt #4
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. English teacher Mr. Okonkwo assigns the common app prompt: 'What do you owe the place that raised you?' Isandro writes something brutally honest at 2 a.m. and, half-asleep, pastes it into his anonymous account instead. It goes viral locally by morning. Beat: the crack where light gets in.

chapters.title: Assigned to Fix You
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Councilwoman Chandrasekaran's daughter is tasked with 'modernizing' the Route 9 homecoming tradition to make the development deal palatable—and to find out who the ghost is. She interviews Isandro, suspecting nothing. Beat: wary attraction disguised as professional interest.

chapters.title: Lanterns in the Attic
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Rosa shows him the attic of the community center: forty years of Route 9 lanterns, photos of families who came home every spring, including his late mother's name on a 1998 lantern. Beat: grief reframed as belonging he didn't know he had.

chapters.title: The Development Deal
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers her mother's deal with the Corliss Group requires Route 9's festival grounds—meaning the tradition must die on paper before anyone notices. She says nothing. Beat: complicity and the first splinter of doubt.

chapters.title: Ghost and Girl
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Isandro and Priya keep meeting—study sessions, diner shifts—while online, @route9ghost starts investigating the Corliss Group. They flirt through arguments about the town's future. Beat: two people falling for each other's better halves.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Days
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A scholarship recruiter visit makes Isandro's exit plan feel real; Rosa quietly panics about the diner. He posts a defense of Route 9 that names the council's 'review committee' without naming his source. Beat: the account stops being commentary and becomes action.

chapters.title: The Leak Hunt
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's mother orders an internal hunt for the leak; Priya realizes she has access to the exact documents the ghost quoted. Suspicion circles her. Beat: terror of being caught in someone else's war.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Out
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro's best friend Dez figures out he's the ghost—not from evidence, but because Isandro cares too much. Instead of exposure, Dez joins him. Beat: the relief of being known, the risk of being known.

chapters.title: The Corliss Man
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A smooth Corliss Group rep offers Priya's family a way out if she publicly endorses the development at the Route 9 preview event. Her mother frames it as protection. Beat: duty tightening like a hand on the wrist.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Last Alibi
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. After a lantern-hanging work night, Isandro and Priya kiss in the community center stairwell—both hiding things from each other in the same breath. Beat: sweetness shadowed by the secret between them.

chapters.title: What the Essay Owed
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Mr. Okonkwo reads Isandro's real college essay and confronts him gently: the essay is about Route 9, and it's true, and it's dangerous. Isandro must decide if honesty is a strategy or a self. Beat: the prompt's question finally lands.

chapters.title: The Preview Event
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At the Corliss showcase, Priya is handed a speech endorsing the development. She reads it—then goes off-script, demanding the town see the actual site plans. Chaos. Beat: the splinter becomes a break.

chapters.title: Retaliation
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The council suspends the Route 9 committee; Rosa's diner lease is terminated early; Dez is threatened with losing his athletic eligibility over 'unrelated' violations. The message is clear. Beat: fear, and the temptation to run.

chapters.title: The Unmasking Threat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The council hires a consultant who traces @route9ghost to the school's network. Priya realizes the suspect list is three names long—and one of them is Isandro. Beat: love against duty, literally.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Priya warns Isandro without saying how she knows. They have until the council vote to save Route 9. Isandro plans a prom-night reveal; Priya must decide whether to testify against her mother. Beat: two people choosing each other and the town at once.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro, Dez, Rosa, and Priya digitize forty years of Route 9 lanterns and homecoming photos into a public archive—every family, every homecoming, every promise kept. Beat: turning nostalgia into evidence, memory into leverage.

chapters.title: Prom Eve
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The eve of the vote and the dance. Priya's mother finds her packing her testimony; their confrontation is raw—duty, immigration sacrifices, love expressed as control. Beat: the cost of choosing, made human on both sides.

chapters.title: The Homecoming of Route 9
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At prom, mid-song, Isandro takes the stage, reveals himself as @route9ghost, and launches the lantern archive on the gym's big screen as families' faces light up around the room. Beat: the climax—invisibility surrendered, identity claimed.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya testifies at the emergency council session, her mother forced to listen. The vote to protect the festival grounds passes by one. Her mother, defeated, says nothing—and that silence is its own beginning. Beat: victory that doesn't feel like winning.

chapters.title: What You Owe
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro submits his college essay—now about choosing to be seen—and gets into his dream school with aid. He and Rosa keep the diner; Dez's eligibility is restored. Beat: the future and the hometown reconciled, not traded.

chapters.title: Lanterns, Lit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring homecoming: Route 9 glows with forty years of lanterns plus new ones, including one for Isandro's mother and one for Priya's family. Isandro posts his last anonymous message—signed with his real name. Beat: coming home as a choice you make, not a place you're stuck.
